title: 石榴果冻材质交互
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Build a single self-contained HTML file: an interactive, physically simulated "Pomegranate Jelly" study in genuine WebGPU + WGSL. Vanilla JS only. No libraries, no external requests, no images or fonts fetched. Everything inline.

CONCEPT
A small, low, curved pomegranate tree made entirely of translucent jelly, standing on a glossy pale-amber jelly plinth in a soft studio. 10–14 ruby-jelly pomegranates hang from it. The user shakes, bends and pulls the tree; fruit fall, and only a hard impact splits one open. A split fruit spills about 30 glossy ruby seeds that behave like a real granular material: they bounce, form little piles, and can be raked around with the cursor. Tone: editorial, quiet, tactile. Think "material study", not a game.

RENDERING (real WebGPU, no WebGL fallback)
- Full-viewport canvas, devicePixelRatio capped at 2. Opaque scene pass into rgba16float with 4x MSAA, depth32.
- Translucent leaves use weighted-blended order-independent transparency (accum + revealage targets). Final composite pass does tonemapping (filmic) plus a little dither noise.
- Soft ground shadow: render coloured transmittance of the tree, fruit and leaves projected along the key light into a small texture, blur it with two separable passes, and sample it on the plinth and backdrop. Shadows are tinted, not grey.
- Backdrop is a warm grey-beige vertical gradient. The studio environment is analytic (a softbox, a warm bounce and a cool fill) and used for reflections and refraction.
- All "jelly" materials share one model: Beer–Lambert absorption by thickness with per-channel sigma, a wrapped diffuse subsurface term, a refracted environment lookup, Fresnel reflection of the studio, and a tight specular glint.
- Plinth: soft rounded slab of pale-amber jelly with a glossy rim.
- Wood: trunk and branches are tapered tubes of warm brown jelly, darker towards the base.
- Leaves: narrow lanceolate, translucent green (OIT), slightly darker midrib, they flutter with the branches. A few can detach when the tree is shaken hard and drift down.
- Pomegranate (ruby jelly): slightly squat round body with a dimpled shoulder and a sunk socket, fine leathery grain, a warm blush toward the shoulder, and seed sacs and membranes faintly glowing through the translucent rind (shader-side 3D cellular noise marched through the body). The 6-sepal crown (calyx) sits at the bottom pole, a short green-brown stem at the top. Each fruit has its own tone and size variation.

PHYSICS (all in JS, fixed timestep, no per-frame allocations)
- The tree is a position-based-dynamics chain/tree with a fixed step of 1/240 s, distance constraints, bend stiffness and damping, anchored at the root. Fruit hang from short stems; the stem tension grows with fruit weight and swing. When the stress exceeds a limit the fruit detaches.
- Detached fruit are free bodies: gravity, the plinth surface, trunk and limb collisions, collisions with each other and with hanging fruit. They roll and rest.
- CRACKING ONLY FROM IMPACT: a free fruit splits when the normal impact speed is above roughly (4.8 − 1.8·ripeness) units/s (floor, trunk and limbs, other fruit). Low drops and gentle rolls never split it. Riper = more fragile.
- When a fruit splits, it becomes two shell halves along a vertical plane through the polar axis. They fly apart sideways, bounce once or twice, rock like a bowl and settle open-side-up. Cap the halves (about 24); the oldest sleeping ones fade out.
- SEEDS: elongated ruby-jelly arils, a few mm across relative to the fruit, with a pale pip glint. Position-based granular simulation, substep 1/120 s, a hashed spatial grid, Coulomb friction (static about 0.7, kinetic about 0.5), small bounce, sleeping and waking so piles stay still and cost nothing. Total soft cap about 400 live seeds (oldest sleepers fade). Seeds also collide with the trunk, the plinth and the shells, and are kept inside a radius around the tree. Soft contact shadows under each seed.
- RAKE: pressing on empty ground near seeds and dragging pushes them with a kinematic cylinder (radius about 0.17, speed-capped) so they pile and spread believably. A thin ring shows the rake under the cursor on hover.

THE CRACKED INTERIOR (must look beautiful, not grey)
The open face of each half is a cut cross-section: a thin red skin edge, then a pale cream pith ring, then dense polished ruby arils (a cellular pattern, 2D Voronoi cells with tiny jitter), each a glossy dome with its own subtle brightness, a dark crease between neighbours, and a faint pale pip. Between the chambers run thin cream membranes (hairlines, not thick walls) radiating from a small pale spongy core. The inside of the shell bowl continues with the same dense ruby beads, with the membrane pattern seen as thin creases. No flat grey or beige anywhere, mostly ruby with a few paler and deeper sacs.

INTERACTION
- Drag a branch or leaf to bend it (the twig follows the pointer with a soft spring).
- Grab a hanging fruit and pull hard: it tears off into your hand. Move and release to throw it. Dropping or flinging it hard enough splits it.
- Pick up a loose fruit again at any time.
- Drag empty space (or right-drag) to orbit; wheel or pinch to zoom, with limits. Touch must work for everything (pointer events, touch-action none).
- Cursor changes: grab / grabbing / pointer over fruit / crosshair over rakeable seeds.

UI: "MATERIAL STUDIES" editorial style
- Warm paper background #ece9e3, ink #241f1d, accent ruby #b3202e. Serif display (Iowan Old Style / Palatino / Georgia stack) for headlines, system sans for controls, mono for numbers.
- Top left: small-caps eyebrow "Material Studies", large italic serif H1 "Pomegranate / Jelly." (two lines), a short rule, caption "A little crack. A little sparkle. A lot of rubies."
- Top right: pill showing a status dot and "WebGPU · Live" (also Paused / Unavailable).
- Right panel (frosted, hairline borders, 268px): section "The tree" with a dark "Shake the tree" button, a thin shake meter, and counters Hanging / Cracked / Seeds. Section "Palette" with three chips: Ruby, Rosé, Amber (each recolours the jelly, tree tint, plinth and shadow tint). Sections with sliders: Firmness, Internal damping, Ripeness (each shows its value). Buttons: Reset, Pause, Reset view.
- Bottom left hint: eyebrow "How to hold it", italic line "Shake it down. Break it open. Rake the rubies.", and small grey text: drag a branch to bend it · pull a fruit and fling it, a hard landing splits it · drag across the seeds to push them · drag empty space or right-drag to orbit · scroll or pinch to zoom.
- Mobile (≤760px): smaller title; the panel becomes a bottom sheet with a "Controls" bar that toggles it; the camera reframes so the tree stays visible above the sheet; the hint and caption fade while it is open; portrait framing pulls the camera back so the whole tree fits.
- If WebGPU is unavailable or the adapter fails: a calm full-screen message in the same typography, and the pill shows "WebGPU · Unavailable". No crashes, no console errors.

QUALITY BAR
- 60 fps on a typical laptop GPU; CPU physics under about 3 ms per frame. Avoid allocations in hot loops. Pause the loop when the tab is hidden.
- No NaNs under any interaction: heavy shaking, many fruit cracking together, resetting mid-drag, resize.
- Reset restores the tree, all fruit, clears halves and seeds.
- Camera defaults: slight three-quarter view, eye height just below the canopy, target on the trunk, the whole tree and the plinth framed with margin.
- Expose a small debug hook (window.__pg) for automated tests.
- Verify in a real browser: tree sways when shaken, fruit detach and crack only on a hard landing, seeds form piles and the rake moves them, all three palettes look right, mobile layout works, no console warnings.

- Pomegranate (ruby jelly): slightly squat round body with a dimpled shoulder and a sunk socket, fine leathery grain, a warm blush toward the shoulder, and seed sacs and membranes faintly glowing through the translucent rind (shader-side 3D cellular noise marched through the body). The 6-sepal crown (calyx) sits at the bottom pole, a short green-brown stem at the top. Each fruit has its own tone and size variation.

- The tree is a position-based-dynamics chain/tree with a fixed step of 1/240 s, distance constraints, bend stiffness and damping, anchored at the root. Fruit hang from short stems; the stem tension grows with fruit weight and swing. When the stress exceeds a limit the fruit detaches.
- Detached fruit are free bodies: gravity, the plinth surface, trunk and limb collisions, collisions with each other and with hanging fruit. They roll and rest.
- CRACKING ONLY FROM IMPACT: a free fruit splits when the normal impact speed is above roughly (4.8 − 1.8·ripeness) units/s (floor, trunk and limbs, other fruit). Low drops and gentle rolls never split it. Riper = more fragile.
- When a fruit splits, it becomes two shell halves along a vertical plane through the polar axis. They fly apart sideways, bounce once or twice, rock like a bowl and settle open-side-up. Cap the halves (about 24); the oldest sleeping ones fade out.
- SEEDS: elongated ruby-jelly arils, a few mm across relative to the fruit, with a pale pip glint. Position-based granular simulation, substep 1/120 s, a hashed spatial grid, Coulomb friction (static about 0.7, kinetic about 0.5), small bounce, sleeping and waking so piles stay still and cost nothing. Total soft cap about 400 live seeds (oldest sleepers fade). Seeds also collide with the trunk, the plinth and the shells, and are kept inside a radius around the tree. Soft contact shadows under each seed.
- RAKE: pressing on empty ground near seeds and dragging pushes them with a kinematic cylinder (radius about 0.17, speed-capped) so they pile and spread believably. A thin ring shows the rake under the cursor on hover.

THE CRACKED INTERIOR (must look beautiful, not grey)
The open face of each half is a cut cross-section: a thin red skin edge, then a pale cream pith ring, then dense polished ruby arils (a cellular pattern, 2D Voronoi cells with tiny jitter), each a glossy dome with its own subtle brightness, a dark crease between neighbours, and a faint pale pip. Between the chambers run thin cream membranes (hairlines, not thick walls) radiating from a small pale spongy core. The inside of the shell bowl continues with the same dense ruby beads, with the membrane pattern seen as thin creases. No flat grey or beige anywhere, mostly ruby with a few paler and deeper sacs.

INTERACTION
- Drag a branch or leaf to bend it (the twig follows the pointer with a soft spring).
- Grab a hanging fruit and pull hard: it tears off into your hand. Move and release to throw it. Dropping or flinging it hard enough splits it.
- Pick up a loose fruit again at any time.
- Drag empty space (or right-drag) to orbit; wheel or pinch to zoom, with limits. Touch must work for everything (pointer events, touch-action none).
- Cursor changes: grab / grabbing / pointer over fruit / crosshair over rakeable seeds.

UI: "MATERIAL STUDIES" editorial style
- Warm paper background #ece9e3, ink #241f1d, accent ruby #b3202e. Serif display (Iowan Old Style / Palatino / Georgia stack) for headlines, system sans for controls, mono for numbers.
- Top left: small-caps eyebrow "Material Studies", large italic serif H1 "Pomegranate / Jelly." (two lines), a short rule, caption "A little crack. A little sparkle. A lot of rubies."
- Top right: pill showing a status dot and "WebGPU · Live" (also Paused / Unavailable).
- Right panel (frosted, hairline borders, 268px): section "The tree" with a dark "Shake the tree" button, a thin shake meter, and counters Hanging / Cracked / Seeds. Section "Palette" with three chips: Ruby, Rosé, Amber (each recolours the jelly, tree tint, plinth and shadow tint). Sections with sliders: Firmness, Internal damping, Ripeness (each shows its value). Buttons: Reset, Pause, Reset view.
- Bottom left hint: eyebrow "How to hold it", italic line "Shake it down. Break it open. Rake the rubies.", and small grey text: drag a branch to bend it · pull a fruit and fling it, a hard landing splits it · drag across the seeds to push them · drag empty space or right-drag to orbit · scroll or pinch to zoom.
- Mobile (≤760px): smaller title; the panel becomes a bottom sheet with a "Controls" bar that toggles it; the camera reframes so the tree stays visible above the sheet; the hint and caption fade while it is open; portrait framing pulls the camera back so the whole tree fits.
- If WebGPU is unavailable or the adapter fails: a calm full-screen message in the same typography, and the pill shows "WebGPU · Unavailable". No crashes, no console errors.

QUALITY BAR
- 60 fps on a typical laptop GPU; CPU physics under about 3 ms per frame. Avoid allocations in hot loops. Pause the loop when the tab is hidden.
- No NaNs under any interaction: heavy shaking, many fruit cracking together, resetting mid-drag, resize.
- Reset restores the tree, all fruit, clears halves and seeds.
- Camera defaults: slight three-quarter view, eye height just below the canopy, target on the trunk, the whole tree and the plinth framed with margin.
- Expose a small debug hook (window.__pg) for automated tests.
- Verify in a real browser: tree sways when shaken, fruit detach and crack only on a hard landing, seeds form piles and the rake moves them, all three palettes look right, mobile layout works, no console warnings.

prompt:
TrackSense is a mission-critical, motorsport-grade time telemetry and predictive analytics platform, designed for Toyota GR Hackathon standards. The following approach ensures technical rigor and award-level UI/UX fidelity.

Design System & Aesthetics
Theme: “Mission Control” + “Motorsport” Jet black/gray backgrounds with a primary accent of #FF4500 (blazing red-orange). Minimal neutral/blue highlights for status indicators only.

Typography:CategoryFontUseHeadingsChakra PetchSquared, geometric, italic or slantedBodyExo 2Futuristic sans, tall x-heightMono/dataJetBrains MonoAll code/data, charts, HUD

Visuals: Avoid PNG/JPG/static SVG imagery. All backgrounds and overlays use HTML5 Canvas or WebGL, driven by props and state for animation consistency.

Core Tech Stack

Framework: React + TypeScript

Styling: Tailwind CSS (w/ custom theme), class-merge for dynamic style shifts
Components: Lucide React Icons (motorsport/tech relevant icons only)
Internal Routing: Single “view” state in App.tsx, e.g., const [view, setView] = useState<'landing'|'dashboard'|'auth'|'team'|'docs'>('landing'); No react-router. All navigation is via handler functions and view state.
Auth Logic: Simulate via localStorage (isAuthed), no real backend.
Animation: All canvas-based animations use strict requestAnimationFrame loops, cancel on unmount.
Dark Mode: Tailwind dark mode is always default and premium; add a toggle for light mode via context/provider.
Global/Reusable Elements
Logo.tsx: Custom SVG: “Chicane” S-curve with a red “Apex” dot; responsive.
Navbar.tsx: Responsive flex, links to Landing, Features, Team, Docs. Theme toggle, Auth/Login button.

TechBackground.tsx: Canvas element. Prop-driven variant: 'circuit'|'grid'|'wave'|'network'|'hex'|'speed' All variants include a persistent “Data Spine” (vertical, center or sidebar) that visually links sections.

Page Component Structure

Landing Page Sections
Hero.tsx: Canvas-powered RacingBackground (3D perspective: rapidly moving track, alternating kerbs, speed particles, “camera shake”). Massive, uppercase, italicized Chakra Petch for main heading: “MASTER THE TRACK”.

Sections: “System Context” — TechBackground variant: 'circuit' “Core Modules” — Heatmap/grid variant, bento grid UI cards “Precision in Milliseconds” — Sine-wave/cosine background, animated sparkline chart “Join the Grid” — Animated network/particle nodes, CTA “Ready to Hack?” — Speed streak visual, call-to-action
Other Pages
Team.tsx: Grid of custom team cards, TechBackground 'hex'
Auth.tsx: RacingBackground (Hero) Glassmorphism modal. Form validation/animated API delay, localStorage simulation.
Dashboard.tsx: Race engineer’s “mission control” bento grid. Ultra-slim nav rail on left; click = update dashboard view. Simulated live data (RPM, Speed, Gear) via useEffect setInterval: Animations for arc gauges, digital readouts Live line charts (react-canvas/ChartCanvas) for throttle/brake/steering SVG vector Fuji Speedway map; animated dot traverses track segment Leaderboard real-time: table with tire icons (Soft, Medium, Hard), sector gap changes AI Console: auto-generated insights log, scrolling terminal
Documentation.tsx: Sidebar nav, scrollable docs, code blocks in JetBrains Mono

Key Code and Performance Fixes

Types: All props, state, and hooks must be strictly typed (no implicit any).

Performance: requestAnimationFrame for all visual updates Canvas/WebGL objects cleaned-up on unmount Simulated data sources throttled to avoid CPU spikes
Accessibility: Sufficient contrast, keyboard accessible nav, alt text for SVG logo

title: 从视频重建三维庭院
author: ericsmith1302
prompt:
"I want you to take the attached video of me slowly rotating around my backyard and build an explorable, photorealistic ThreeJS model of the entire space.

The model should reconstruct the actual geometry of my backyard from the video with extremely accurate spatial reasoning. The house, patio, fence, trees, landscaping, grass, elevation changes, furniture, and every other visible element should be positioned and scaled as accurately as possible.

Do not just wrap the video around a sphere or create a fake panoramic environment. I need a real 3D scene that I can freely walk around and view from angles that were not shown directly in the video.

Use the frames from the video as textures wherever possible, but correctly project and perspective-correct them onto actual 3D geometry so they do not look stretched or distorted when I move around.

Fan out sub-agents to separately handle:

- video frame extraction and analysis
- camera position and lens estimation
- depth estimation
- spatial layout reconstruction
- house and patio geometry
- fence and yard boundaries
- terrain and elevation changes
- trees and landscaping
- texture extraction and projection
- lighting
- ThreeJS implementation
- first-person movement and collision
- visual validation against the original video

Have multiple sub-agents independently create competing estimates of the backyard layout, then have another sub-agent compare them against the video and determine which reconstruction is most spatially accurate.

You should /loop on the geometry until the model matches the video from every recoverable camera angle.

Have a separate harsh critic sub-agent repeatedly render the ThreeJS scene from the same camera positions as frames from the source video and compare them side by side.

The critic should check whether:

- every major object appears in the correct position
- distances and proportions are accurate
- fence lines and house angles align
- trees and landscaping line up
- occlusion matches
- terrain slope matches
- textures align with the geometry
- nothing floats, intersects, stretches, or looks like a flat projection

If the reconstruction does not line up extremely closely with the original video, reject it and keep iterating.

Do not stop at a rough approximation.

Do not stop when it merely looks impressive from the starting viewpoint.

It must remain spatially coherent and convincing when I walk around the scene.

Where the video does not provide enough information, use the strongest available combination of perspective analysis, depth estimation, object-size priors, architectural reasoning, and consistency across frames. Keep uncertain dimensions configurable so they can be adjusted later.

Build this as a complete ThreeJS web app with:

- first-person controls
- orbit controls
- collision
- realistic lighting and shadows
- a reset button returning me to the original filming position
- saved viewpoints matching key frames from the video
- a top-down view of the reconstructed backyard
- editable measurements for uncertain dimensions

/loop on every major part of the scene.

Have the harsh critic compare the finished result blindly against the original video frames and keep rejecting it until the reconstruction is as visually and spatially accurate as the available footage allows.

Fan out sub-agents, ultrathink, ultracode, validate visually, and do not stop until the backyard feels like a genuine 3D digital twin rather than a panorama or generic approximation.

Additionally, I want there to be a chat interface where I can talk with an LLM that can produce any 3D asset on the fly and add it to the scene.

Alternative stop criteria: If you have been working for more than 60 minutes with unsatisfactory results, wrap up and finish."

title: 三维直升机产品展示
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Create a detailed, interactive 3D scene of a modern helicopter in a single HTML file using Three.js and WebGL. Build genuine 3D geometry that can be viewed from every angle, not an image.

Visual style:
A premium aviation design presentation with a light gray studio background, a circular display platform, soft shadows, and realistic reflections.
Helicopter:

A smooth, streamlined fuselage inspired by light twin-engine helicopters such as the H145.
A white body with a dark navy underside and blue accent stripe.
Curved, tinted cockpit windows with reflections and carefully fitted window seals.
Side doors, handles, panel seams, rivets, boarding steps, and antennas.
Two engine housings with air intakes, ventilation grilles, and exhaust outlets.
A five-bladed main rotor with a detailed hub, attachment hardware, and pitch-control linkages.
A tapered tail boom, stabilizers, and a shrouded tail rotor with a genuine opening through its housing.
Curved landing skids attached to the fuselage with structural supports.
Navigation lights and a blinking beacon.
All components must connect physically. Avoid floating parts, gaps between sections, rotor blades intersecting the fuselage, or windows hovering above the body.

Interactions:

Mouse drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, and touch controls.
Start and stop both rotors with gradual acceleration and deceleration.
Adjustable rotor speed.
Hover mode: smoothly lift off the platform, gently sway in the air, and land softly when disabled.
Automatic camera orbit.
Front, side, and tail camera presets.
Reset camera and fullscreen controls.
Three liveries: glacier blue and white, rescue orange, and graphite.
Interface:

Top left: a small “AERONAUT / OBJECT STUDIES” label and a large “Horizon 05.” heading.
Right side: a compact panel with specifications, helicopter status, livery selection, and rotor speed.
Bottom: controls and interaction hints.
Restrained typography, thin borders, and generous whitespace. Keep the helicopter unobstructed.
All interface text in English.
Technical requirements:

Generate the geometry procedurally without downloading a prebuilt helicopter model.
Use PBR materials, a studio reflection environment, and soft shadows.
Make animation independent of frame rate.
Reuse geometry and materials where appropriate, and cap pixel ratio for performance.
Support desktop and mobile layouts, keeping the full rotor span visible in the initial view.
If possible, embed dependencies in the HTML so the file works offline.
Display a helpful fallback message if WebGL is unavailable.
Before finishing, inspect the model from every side, test every control, and check for console errors. Pay particular attention to the silhouette, structural connections, glazing, and rotor mechanisms.

Deliver the working HTML file, not just an explanation.

title: 龙卷风互动场景
author: ivanainai
prompt:
Build a complete, working, cinematic 3D browser scene: a powerful tornado crossing a golden wheat field and tearing the roof off a weathered barn.

Use Three.js/WebGL. Implement and run the experience in the available preview. If no preview is available, deliver a runnable project with clear launch instructions. Do not stop at a description, storyboard or code outline.

This is an interactive real-time graphics demonstration with stylized physics, not a scientifically accurate weather simulation.

ART DIRECTION

Aim for a cinematic storm scene with natural materials, atmospheric depth and convincing scale.

Golden wheat fills the foreground. A weathered red timber barn stands in the middle distance, beside a narrow dirt track and a few fence posts. Beyond it, a massive charcoal storm cloud hangs low over the landscape.

Warm, low sunlight enters from the left, illuminating wheat, dust and the edges of airborne debris. The storm behind the tornado is much darker. Keep shadows readable.

The tornado is the dominant subject. Frame it from a low three-quarter perspective, with wheat close to the camera and the funnel extending high into the storm. Keep the barn large enough that its destruction is legible on a phone.

No cartoon colors, low-poly aesthetic, wireframes, glowing particles or sci-fi effects.

THE TORNADO

Make a living, irregular funnel, broad at cloud level and narrow near the ground. Its centerline should lean and slowly bend. Its silhouette should fluctuate as it rotates.

Construct convincing visual volume using layered, softly shaded particles or another performant technique. Use procedurally generated soft textures if needed. Avoid a solid cone, a stack of visible rings, hard-edged sprites or a hollow wire cage.

Use darker condensation above and warm brown dust at ground level. The dust skirt should spread across the field and partially obscure the base.

Particle motion must combine rotation, inward attraction, rising motion and turbulence. Inner regions rotate faster. Vary particle size, opacity and angular speed so the whole funnel does not rotate like one rigid object.

Add sparse straw and identifiable pieces of debris. Large objects should remain easy to follow.

THE WHEAT

Render a dense field efficiently using instancing. Suggest wheat heads and stalks with economical geometry.

Normal wind creates broad, coherent waves across the field.

Near the tornado, stalks bend strongly toward the swirling wind. As it passes, leave an irregular flattened track that remains visible for the rest of the sequence.

Use a persistent world-space damage field or an equivalent efficient approach. Avoid updating every stalk on the CPU each frame.

THE BARN

Build the barn from separate structural elements so its destruction follows what the viewer sees.

The approaching wind first shakes loose roof panels. One panel lifts at an edge, peels upward and detaches. Several additional panels and a few timber pieces follow.

Keep some of the barn standing so the damage is obvious.

Give debris gravity, angular velocity and wind influence. Nearby light pieces can spiral upward; heavier pieces should travel lower and fall back to the ground. Prevent visible debris from passing through the terrain.

The tornado’s proximity and wind strength should trigger destruction. Do not make the barn explode into random particles.

AUTOMATIC 20-SECOND SHOT

The opening frame must already show a fully formed tornado touching down and wheat bending. No introduction, fade-in or waiting for the funnel to form.

0–4 seconds:

prompt:
-

Create a cinematic, 3D interactive football website where the user controls one iconic free-kick moment.
The experience should feel like a AAA football game intro mixed with a premium WebGL website.

The site must be smooth, minimal, emotional, and physics-accurate.

ART DIRECTION & MOOD

Tone: Epic, focused, high-stakes

Visual style:

Dark, cinematic stadium lighting

Strong contrast between player, ball, and goal

Volumetric light beams from floodlights

Color grading:

Night match: deep blues & whites

Rain mode: cold tones, reflections

UCL mode: royal blue + gold accents

No clutter, no UI overload

3D SCENE SETUP

Fullscreen WebGL canvas

Scene contains:

Football pitch (realistic grass shader)

Stadium with animated crowd silhouettes

Goal net with physics-based deformation

High-detail football model (normal + roughness maps)

Camera:

Cinematic third-person angle

Smooth easing on all movements

 CORE INTERACTIONS (MANDATORY)
AIMING (Mouse Drag)

User drags mouse horizontally & vertically

This defines:

Shot direction

Curve direction (left / right bend)

Display:

Subtle ghost trajectory line (fades in/out)

Ball slightly rotates while aiming

Camera slightly shifts based on aim direction (parallax feel)

POWER BUILDUP (Scroll)

Mouse wheel / trackpad scroll increases shot power

Visual feedback:

Energy ring builds around the ball

Grass particles subtly lift

Stadium sound intensifies

Power capped to prevent unrealistic shots

UI remains minimal (no bars, only visual cues)

 SHOT RELEASE (Click / Release)

On release:

Enter slow motion (0.2x speed)

Player foot strikes ball

Impact compression on ball mesh

Sound:

Clean kick impact

Crowd inhale silence before the shot

 BALL PHYSICS (CRITICAL)

Realistic physics simulation:

Magnus effect for curve shots

Knuckle shot = unstable air drag

Power shot = minimal curve, high velocity

Spin visibly affects ball trajectory

Ball shadow dynamically follows pitch

 CINEMATIC CAMERA FOLLOW

Camera locks onto ball mid-air

Smooth spline-based camera movement

Dynamic FOV shift for speed sensation

Camera shake on powerful shots (subtle)

GOAL IMPACT & NET REACTION

Net reacts with soft-body physics

Net ripples in slow motion

Ball pushes net backward realistically

Crowd reaction fades in after goal impact

Light bloom increases briefly on goal
 EXTRA MODES (TOGGLEABLE)

Shot Types

Knuckle Shot

Curve Shot

Power Shot

Each mode affects:

Physics

Ball spin

Camera intensity

Sound profile

Stadium Atmospheres

Night Match

Heavy Rain (wet pitch reflections)

Champions League Final (anthem ambience)

Each mode changes:

Lighting

Crowd intensity

Environmental effects

ANIMATIONS & MOTION RULES

All transitions must use:

Ease-in-out

Spring-based motion where possible

No sudden cuts

Minimum 60 FPS target

Slow motion used only once per shot

TECH REQUIREMENTS

Three.js or React Three Fiber

Physics engine (Cannon / Ammo / custom)

GSAP or native RAF loops

Shaders for:

Grass

Ball surface

Light bloom

Fully responsive

Graceful fallback for low-end devices

USER EXPERIENCE PRINCIPLE

The user must feel like they caused the goal, not just watched it.

No tutorials.
The interaction should feel instinctive.

FINAL FEELING

Short

Replayable

Addictive

Premium

Share-worthy

The website should feel like:

“I want to try that shot again.”

DO NOT

Do not add scoreboards

Do not add ads

Do not add unnecessary UI

Do not overload text

author: shmopixbzn
prompt:
Build “Plush Octopus”, a single-file interactive WebGPU experience with a WebGL 2 fallback.
Design: Use a warm ivory background, muted coral and sage accents, thin borders, generous whitespace, and a large italic serif title: “Plush / Octopus.” Add the small kicker “Material Studies / No. 022.” Keep text minimal and the UI in English. No studio branding. Place the octopus on the left and a compact control panel on the right. Make the layout responsive for mobile.
Octopus: Create the entire toy procedurally—no imported 3D models. Give it a softly sagging mantle, eight tapered curling arms, heavy-lidded button eyes, a small side siphon, and two rows of cream-colored suckers beneath each arm. Use soft velvet shading with subtle directional nap and gentle blush waves. Avoid harsh speckles or flickering surface noise.
Physics: Make it feel like a lightly stuffed, jelly-like plush. The mantle should squash, spread sideways while preserving volume, and wobble briefly after release. Use a surface-net mesh driven by an XPBD soft-body lattice. Keep deformation centered so it cannot create unwanted sideways motion. Arms should bend smoothly and retain their shape like soft wire, with stable length constraints even during fast dragging. Include gravity, floor friction, and breakable sucker adhesion.
Interactions:
Hand: Lift, squash, release, and bend individual arms. Held arms gradually wrap around the hand.
Finger: Attract an arm; tapping the mantle makes the octopus briefly startle and pale.
Brush: Stroke the velvet to change its nap.
Actions: Crawl, Hide, Reach, Blush, Smooth nap, Reset.
Sliders: Stuffing, Wire stiffness, Grip.
Palettes: Coral, Dusk, Sea glass.
Include quarter-speed and mesh toggles, a live status indicator, and compact Mass, Volume, Grip, and Blushes readouts.
Animation and rendering: Add slow breathing, occasional blinking, and independent tip movement. Use fixed simulation steps with render interpolation and smoothly blended behaviors. Motion must settle naturally without perpetual rocking, snapping, stretching, or tube-frame flips.
Render one continuous, soft floor shadow that follows the body and arms. Prevent visible circular shadow stamps, dark overlap patches, and depth artifacts. Shadows should broaden and fade as the octopus rises.
Deliver one self-contained HTML file. Aim for smooth 60 fps on capable devices and test idle stability, extreme arm pulls, squash-and-release, lifting, behavior transitions, and mobile input.

title: 滑雪度假村滚动叙事网站
author: exploraX_
prompt:
Build a complete, scroll-scrubbed animated winter ski resort website called **KAMMHORN — Swiss Alpine Ski & Expedition Sanctuary** using the `scroll-world` continuous camera-flight architecture and Higgsfield image/video generation.

### 1. Brand, Art Direction & Color Palette
- **Brand Name**: KAMMHORN (3,420m · Valais Canton · Swiss Alps)
- **Visual Style**: Mid-century Swiss alpine travel poster illustration (inspired by Emil Cardinaux, Martin Peikert, and classic 1950s Swissair/Zermatt lithographs). Crisp geometric rock facets, warm cream sunlit snow planes, cool glacier-blue shadows, deep navy spruce silhouettes, and bold crimson-red focal accents. Zero text or watermarks baked into any generated image or video.
- **Color Palette**:
  - Alpenglow Cream (`#F4EFE6`) — primary display typography & sunlit snow highlights
  - Powder Sky (`#9EC1D9`) — upper atmosphere & secondary labels
  - Glacier Slate (`#5B84A8`) — mountain shadow facets & ice walls
  - Deep Pine Navy (`#1B2D42` / `#0F1B29`) — background, frosted glass cards, & foreground pine silhouettes
  - Gondola Crimson (`#D93829`) — primary CTA buttons, active states, cabin & jacket accents
  - Lantern Amber (`#E89B3C`) — twilight lanterns & chalet hearth glow
- **Typography**:
  - Monumental Hero Display: `Cinzel` / `Fraunces` (900 weight, uppercase, tight tracking)
  - Section Titles: `Fraunces` (serif display)
  - Body Copy & Controls: `Plus Jakarta Sans`
  - Telemetry & Coordinates: `JetBrains Mono`

---

### 2. Six-Chapter Continuous Camera Journey (Story Beats)
Build 6 connected scenes where the camera descends from the 3,420m summit down to the 1,620m timber base lodge, with continuous active motion inside every scene:

1. **01 · Express Aerial Ski Lift (`lift` — 3,420m)**
   - *Scene*: Iconic crimson-red aerial cable car suspended on steel cables high above snow-covered spruce ridges, ascending toward a jagged sunlit alpine peak.
   - *Motion*: The red gondola glides steadily upward-right along the cable; cables sway subtly; clouds and snow crystals drift past.
   - *Copy*: "Rise Above the Timberline."
2. **02 · Alpine Downhill Skiing (`skiing` — 2,980m)**
   - *Scene*: Wide sun-drenched glacier bowl and groomed corduroy pistes beneath the same faceted alpine peak.
   - *Motion*: Three skiers in crimson jackets and dark navy pants carve rhythmic S-turns down the slope, kicking up backlit plumes of dry powder snow.
   - *Copy*: "Carve the Morning Corduroy."
3. **03 · Freestyle Snowboarding (`snowboard` — 2,640m)**
   - *Scene*: Sculpted 22-foot alpine superpipe and terrain park kickers framed by jagged blue mountain ridges.
   - *Motion*: A snowboarder in a burnt-crimson jacket launches high off the lip of the halfpipe in a grab trick with an arc of glittering snow spray trailing the board.
   - *Copy*: "Built for Airtime & Flow."
4. **04 · Glacier Ice Climbing (`iceclimb` — 2,310m)**
   - *Scene*: Towering vertical frozen waterfall and crystalline blue glacier seracs in Eisfall Gorge.
   - *Motion*: Two mountaineers in crimson shells on belay swing technical ice axes and kick crampons up the vertical blue ice column, sending glittering ice shards downward.
   - *Copy*: "Vertical Blue Ice."
5. **05 · Lantern Snowshoeing (`snowshoe` — 1,940m)**
   - *Scene*: Arched timber footbridge crossing a frozen creek inside a hushed spruce forest at golden-hour twilight.
   - *Motion*: A small group of snowshoers carrying warm glowing amber lanterns walks steadily across the snowy wooden bridge while gentle snowflakes drift through the pines.
   - *Copy*: "Into the Quiet Woods."
6. **06 · Base Chalet & Après-Ski (`chalet` — 1,620m)**
   - *Scene*: Warm glowing timber alpine ski lodge at dusk with snow-laden roofs, a roaring outdoor stone firepit, and the crimson gondola gliding home overhead.
   - *Motion*: Golden flames and embers dance in the stone firepit, silver woodsmoke curls from the stone chimney into the alpenglow sky, and warm lodge windows shimmer.
   - *Copy*: "Your Mountain Table Is Waiting." (Includes primary CTA to open the Winter Pass Booking Modal).

---

### 3. Dual Aspect-Ratio Higgsfield Pipeline & Seam Verification
Generate two native video chains — **Desktop (`16:9`, `1280×720`)** and **Native Mobile (`9:16` portrait, `720×1280`)**:
1. **Anchor Reference**: Use the hero gondola illustration (`assets/hero-ref.jpg`) as `--image` reference when generating all 6 scene stills (`gpt_image_2` or `nano_banana_pro`) so every scene shares identical brushwork, palette, and mountain geometry.
2. **Exact-Match Seamless Chaining**:
   - Each clip `i` is generated with `seedance_2_0_mini` (`5s`) using scene `i`'s start plate (`--image`) and scene `i+1`'s start plate (`--end-image`) so the camera continuously flies from scene `i` into scene `i+1` while subjects move dynamically inside the frame.
   - Extract the final frame of clip `i` and compare it numerically against the first frame of clip `i+1` (`ffmpeg -lavfi "blend=all_mode=difference,showinfo"`). Every seam on both Desktop (`16:9`) and Mobile (`9:16`) must have a mean pixel difference `< 8`.
3. **Scrub-Ready Encoding**:
   - Desktop clips (`assets/vid/<name>.mp4`): `-vf "scale=1280:720,fps=24" -c:v libx264 -profile:v high -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 20 -g 8 -keyint_min 1 -sc_threshold 0 -bf 0 -an -movflags +faststart`
   - Mobile portrait clips (`assets/vid/<name>-m.mp4`): `-vf "scale=720:1280,fps=24" -c:v libx264 -profile:v main -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 22 -g 4 -keyint_min 1 -sc_threshold 0 -bf 0 -an -movflags +faststart`
   - Extract first-frame WebP posters (`assets/<name>.webp` and `assets/<name>-m.webp`) and 6 service card thumbnails (`assets/gallery-<name>.webp`).

---

### 4. Multi-Plane "Moving Objects" Canvas System & Editorial UI
Inspired by classic layered travel posters ("VISITE" / Notosan layout):
1. **Monumental Layered Hero (`#heroEditorial`)**:
   - Full-width display title `KAMMHORN` with kicker `01 / SUMMIT EXPRESS GONDOLA · 3,420M`, frosted glass description card, `Start the journey ▶` button (smooth-jumps to Scene 2), and `Book Winter Pass · CHF 89` CTA.
2. **Two Real-Time 2D Canvases Around the Typography**:
   - `#sceneObjectsCanvas` (`z-index: 15`, behind typography):
     - Flocking alpine chough birds with sinusoidal wingbeats gliding across the peaks.
     - Soft mid-century illustrated cloud banks drifting horizontally with scroll-linked parallax.
     - An auxiliary miniature crimson gondola gliding along an upper cable in Scene 1.
     - Swaying deep-navy foreground pine silhouettes framing the bottom left/right corners.
     - Rising golden firepit embers in Scene 6 (`chalet`).
   - `#cloudOverlapCanvas` (`z-index: 29`, in front of `#heroEditorial` typography):
     - Translucent mist ribbons and foreground birds that pass directly *over* the giant `KAMMHORN` letters for true multi-plane depth.
     - Scroll-velocity-reactive snow & spindrift particles.
3. **Interactive Resort Chrome & Below-the-Fold Guide**:
   - **Top Bar**: Brand badge (`KAMMHORN · 3,420M`), 6-button pill nav (`Ski Lift`, `Skiing`, `Snowboarding`, `Ice Climbing`, `Snowshoeing`, `Base Chalet`) synced to active scroll section, and `RESERVE PASS` button.
   - **Right Route Rail**: Vertical progress dots + active section badge.
   - **Bottom-Left Live Telemetry HUD**: Pulsing green live dot + real-time `SECTOR`, `ELEVATION`, `CONDITIONS`, and `MOVING ACTIVITY` updated per chapter.
   - **Below-the-Fold Resort Guide**: 6-card responsive grid showcasing all six mountain services with operating hours, elevation badges, and direct booking triggers.
   - **Interactive Winter Pass Booking Modal**: Allows guests to select their service/pass tier, date, and party size with instant reservation confirmation.

---

### 5. Responsive & Accessibility Requirements
- Automatically serve `16:9` clips/posters on Desktop (`> 860px`) and native `9:16` portrait clips/posters on Mobile (`<= 860px`), including live switching on viewport resize.
- Preload all video clips into in-memory `blob:` URLs before assigning `video.src` so scroll-scrubbing via `requestAnimationFrame` (`currentTime` LERP `0.22`) has zero network stalls.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` by disabling video scrubbing and canvas particle loops and displaying the crisp illustrated WebP stills.

title: 单文件王国历史模拟
author: emollick
prompt:
ANNALS — a living kingdom in a single file

Working title behavior: the app titles itself per seed — "The Annals of Vaelmere", "The Annals of Osterholt" — because the central conceit is that you are watching a history write itself. The kingdom is the simulation; the Chronicle is the soul.

1. Vision

A procedurally generated fantasy kingdom rendered in real-time 3D that you can watch for five minutes or five hours. Zoom from a satellite view of the whole realm down to a market stall with laundry on the line. Time runs; harvests come in; caravans crawl the roads; a queen dies without a clear heir and two great houses raise banners; plague follows the trade routes; a dragon notices the treasury has gotten large. Everything that happens is written into a scrolling Chronicle in the voice of a medieval annalist, and a cinematic auto-director flies the camera to the story as it unfolds.

Four pillars, in priority order:

Legible emergence. Systems couple visibly: drought → failed harvest → hunger → unrest → rebellion. A viewer should be able to reconstruct cause from effect just by watching.

Zoom is the reward. Every altitude has something worth seeing — political geography at 3 km, trade arteries at 800 m, street life at 40 m.
The Chronicle is the product. Named people, named places, consequences that persist (ruins, grudges, epithets). The sim generates a story you could retell.
Watchable by default. With zero input it should behave like a nature documentary about a kingdom.
2. Hard constraints

Single HTML file, vanilla JS + Three.js from CDN (write against the r128 API surface so the same file runs as a Claude artifact during development and unchanged on Netlify). No build step, no framework, no backend.

Custom camera controller (no OrbitControls dependency — we need a bespoke rig anyway, see §5).

No localStorage / sessionStorage. Persistence is the seed: URL hash #s=1234567 fully determines the generated world. "Copy link" button shares it. Optional "Export chronicle" downloads a .txt.
Deterministic worldgen via seeded sfc32 RNG with separate streams for generation and history, so intervening in history never changes the map.
Performance floor: 60 fps on a mid-tier laptop at every altitude; <250 draw calls via instancing and merged geometry; graceful degradation, never a crash.
Everything procedural — no external textures or models. Vertex colors, tiny generated canvas atlases (windows, sigils), and shader work carry the visuals.
3. World generation pipeline
Runs once per seed, in order, with a brief "forging the realm" progress line:

Terrain. 6×6 km world. fBm heightmap with domain warping; one mountain spine, rolling lowlands, ~40% of seeds get a coastline on one edge.

Hydrology. Flow accumulation carves one major river (always) plus tributaries; lakes in basins; river mouths become harbor candidates.

Biomes. Moisture × elevation → meadow, farmland-suitable plain, deciduous forest, pine upland, rocky peak, marsh. Drives tree instancing, ground vertex color, and resource nodes (farmland, forest, ore vein in rock, fishing water).

Settlement siting. Score cells by water access, flat buildable area, resource adjacency, harbor bonus. Place 1 capital (pop ~2,500), 2–3 towns (400–1,200), 3–5 villages (60–300). Capital gets a keep on defensible high ground and a walled old core.
King's roads. A* over a cost field (slope² penalty, water crossing penalty that spawns bridges, forest penalty) connecting all settlements into a network. Roads are the circulatory system — trade, armies, plague, and bandits all use them.
Streets & lots. Inside settlements, organic street growth seeded from the road entry points and the market square; lots subdivide along streets; districts assigned (market, artisan, residential, temple, keep). Villages are a crossroads, a well, and a cluster.
Buildings. ~2,500–4,500 total from 12 archetypes × 3 tiers (hovel→timber→stone): house, longhouse, shop, smithy, mill (animated wheel on watercourses), granary, tavern, temple, warehouse, tower, wall segment/gate, keep. Procedural assembly: footprint, floors, roof style, chimneys, timber-frame overlay at tier 2+, hanging signs on shops.
Names & heraldry. One coherent phonology: places from syllable banks with earthy suffixes (-mere, -ford, -holt, -caster, -wyck); people from gendered given-name banks; great houses take a place or beast name. Procedural sigils = field color pair + one charge from a bank of 16 (stag, tower, wave, oak, wolf, comet, key, sun…), rendered to a small canvas atlas and used on keep banners, army flags, and UI chips.
The cast. Crown dynasty (monarch, consort, children) + 5 great houses, each holding a region and seat. ~100–140 living notables at any time (see §7).
4. Rendering, LOD & visual style
Aesthetic: illuminated-manuscript storybook. Low-poly forms with painterly vertex-color gradients — not flat-shaded minimalism, not photorealism. The world should look like the marginalia of a chronicle came to life. One directional sun/moon light with a tight camera-tracking shadow frustum (shadows fade out above 1,500 m altitude), height + distance fog for depth, custom gradient sky dome with sun, moon, stars, and the occasional comet.
Water: gerstner-lite vertex displacement + fresnel tint on rivers, lakes, sea. Rivers visibly swell during floods.

Day/night: full cycle; nights are deep indigo with warm emissive windows (per-instance emissive flag in the bubble band), pooled torch/lamp point lights (≤12), keep braziers.

Seasons (90 days each, 360-day year): global palette lerp + effects. Spring: saturated greens, snowmelt-fat rivers. Summer: warm golds (drought pushes to straw-yellow). Autumn: russet forest ramp. Winter: snow accumulation via normal-up whitening in the ground/roof shaders, snowfall particles, frozen lake tint.

Weather: clear/overcast/rain/storm/snow state machine; rain streak particles, wet-darkened ground tint, storm lightning flashes. Weather is mechanical, not just decorative (fire spread, battle modifiers, flood meter).

Ambient life: chimney smoke curls, birds (cheap boid flock), grazing sheep sprites near farms, banner cloth idle-wave shader, market crowd murmur of villagers in the bubble band.
LOD bands (camera distance to object):
Band Range Buildings Agents Detail     Far >2,200 m merged/instanced color-block masses per district armies → banner icon, caravans → moving dot settlement name labels, territory tint   Mid 500–2,200 m instanced archetype meshes full low-poly agent meshes instanced trees, roads, bridges   Near 120–500 m + chimneys, signs, timber overlays walk-bob animation wells, carts, market stalls   Bubble <120 m + per-instance window glow, laundry lines, lamps citizens spawn (≤80), individual heads turn prop shadows, torch lights
Citizens outside the bubble do not exist as entities — they're statistics (§7). The bubble makes the zoom promise real without simulating 8,000 pedestrians.
UI skin: parchment panel (#E9DCC3) with iron-gall ink text (#2B2320), crown-gold accents (#C9A227), house colors from sigils. Chronicle set in a period serif (IM Fell English or similar via Google Fonts, with graceful serif fallback); UI labels in a clean humanist sans. Trigger buttons read like acts, sentence case, active voice: "Unleash plague," "Bless the harvest," "Contest the succession."

5. Camera & interaction
Custom rig with three modes, all sharing one smoothed spring-damper transform:
Free: orbit + pan + scroll zoom along a curved altitude path — high altitude looks steeper (map-like), low altitude tilts toward the horizon (street-like). Zoom range ~5 m to ~4,000 m. Terrain collision keeps the camera out of the ground.
Follow: click any agent (caravan, army, notable, dragon) → low tracking shot with slight lead. Click empty ground to release.
Director: see §13.
Raycast click on anything selectable opens the Inspector (§15). Hotkeys: Space pause, 1–4 speeds, H hide UI, C Watch mode, Esc deselect.
6. Simulation architecture
Clock: SimClock in fractional days. Fixed-step accumulator; 1 tick = 1 sim-day of system logic. Speeds: pause / 0.5 / 2 / 8 / 30 sim-days per real second (at max, a year passes in 12 seconds — a monarch's reign in ~10 minutes).
System order per tick: Weather → Economy → Population → Politics → Military → Threats → Growth → Chronicle flush.
Render decoupling: agents store path + departure/arrival sim-times; the render loop interpolates positions every frame from current sim-time, so motion is smooth at any speed and nothing "teleports."
Stability rule: every positive feedback loop ships with a predator. Growth ↑ → land scarcity and food pressure. Treasury ↑ → dragon and bandit attention. Military strength ↑ → upkeep drain. House power ↑ → crown suspicion events. Target: after 200 unattended sim-years at defaults, population and treasury remain within sane bounds and the realm is still interesting.
Pacing target: a Chronicle-worthy event every 15–45 sim-days at default rates (tunable via the Disaster frequency and House aggression sliders).
7. Population & notables
Two-layer model (the Crusader Kings trick):
Pools: each settlement tracks population as a number with birth/death/migration rates modified by food, plague, war, prosperity. Pools drive building growth, levy size, tax income, and bubble-band citizen density.
Notables: ~100–140 named characters — the dynasty, house heads and their families, plus flavor roles (High Priest, Master of Coin, a famous smith, a bandit king when one arises, a prophet at Myth High). Notables have: age, sex, house, 2 traits (from ~16: bold/craven, just/cruel, shrewd/dull, pious/cynical, fertile, sickly…), relationships (spouse, heirs, grudges), and an agenda line. They age, marry (arranged for alliance value), have children, and die by an age hazard curve plus event hazards (battle, plague, childbirth, the occasional hunting accident, assassination). Deaths and births are Chronicle events; important ones are Director beats.
8. Economy & trade
Legibility over realism. Seven goods: grain, fish, timber, ore, tools, cloth, wine.
Settlements produce by geography (farmland → grain, forest → timber, ore vein → ore, harbor → fish; towns convert ore+timber → tools, capital produces cloth/wine), consume by population, and store in granaries/warehouses.
Local prices from stock vs. need; caravans (mule train meshes, up to ~36 concurrent) spawn to arbitrage price gaps along roads; coastal cogs (up to 8) trade between harbor settlements. Trade volume is visible traffic — the kingdom's health readable at a glance.
Treasury: crown taxes trade and harvests (default 12%); spends on army upkeep, disaster relief, bounties, rebuilding. Treasury funds war; war disrupts trade; disrupted trade starves treasuries.
Hunger cascade: food deficit → granary drawdown → hunger → mortality up, unrest up, migration out. Drought, plague, siege, and raided caravans all feed this one legible pipeline.
9. Dynasty, houses & politics
Succession: gender-blind primogeniture. Heirs need to survive to inherit; a monarch dying with no adult heir triggers a regency (unrest up, house aggression up) or, with rival claimants, a succession crisis.
Legitimacy (0–100) on the crown: raised by coronations, victories, festivals, dragon-slaying; lowered by lost wars, famines under their rule, assassinations, dark omens at Myth High.
House loyalty (0–100 each): drifts with tax rate, shared wars, royal marriages (arranged automatically for alliance value; weddings are festival events), slights and grudges (event-driven), and monarch traits.
Unrest per settlement from hunger, taxes, war, plague, omens → riots (small fires, trade pause) → revolt (settlement flips banner) at extremes.
Civil war trigger: loyalty <30 on a house with military strength + a spark (succession crisis, famine year, tax hike, "Contest the succession" button). Houses declare for sides based on loyalty, marriages, and grudges. Territory overlay animates as banners change.
10. War
Armies: levies raised from settlement pools (strength = f(population, prosperity, walls)); an army is one entity rendered as up to ~300 instanced soldiers with banner (banner-blob icon beyond 800 m). Armies march along roads at ~15 km/sim-day, eat supply, and are gorgeous to follow in Follow cam.
Battles: armies within contact on the same route → 2-sim-day abstract resolution in three phases (skirmish/clash/rout) with visible melee shuffle, arrow arcs, dust, and casualties trickling both pools. Great fire: ignition (lightning, riot, sack, drunk smith, trigger) spreads through the building adjacency graph, biased by density, dryness (drought!), and wind direction; rain suppresses. Burned lots → charred ruins → rebuild timer gated on prosperity.
Flood: winter snowpack meter; heavy melt + spring storms swell the river 1.5× width, damaging riverside lots and bridges.
Drought: summer event; harvest ×0.4, grass palette to straw, fire dryness up → feeds the hunger cascade.

Earthquake: rare; camera shake, 2–8% of buildings near epicenter to rubble, secondary fires.

A scrolling parchment panel writing dated entries in annalist voice via a template grammar with slots, tone variants, and occasional editorializing ("…and some say the comet foretold it"). Entry classes: births/deaths/marriages/coronations, harvests and famines, trade and founding, war declarations/battles/sieges/peaces, disasters, omens, bandit and dragon affairs, festivals.
Every entry is clickable → camera flies to the location (if it still stands; else to the ruin or cairn).

Reign headers divide the scroll: "Here begin the years of Queen Maelis, second of her name."

Filter chips (Crown / War / Trade / Fates). Export button saves the full annals as .txt — a shareable artifact of the run.

Core is fully local (no API). Optional enhancement when running as a Claude artifact: a "Illuminate this entry" button that expands one entry into a paragraph via the API — omitted from the Netlify build.

The feature that makes it fascinating to watch. An event bus emits beats with priorities (dragon raid 10, war declared 10, coronation 9, battle 8, great fire 8, plague arrival 7, royal wedding 6, founding 6, caravan ambush 5, festival 3). The director:

Uses shot grammar: wide establishing → push-in on the subject; low tracking shots for marches and caravans; slow orbit for sieges and festivals; high wide for territory flips.

Renders a lower-third beat card with the Chronicle line for the current shot.

Slider Governs     Harvest yield food production   Birth rate / Mortality population pool dynamics   Trade volume caravan/cog spawn rate   Tax rate (5–30%, default 12%) treasury vs. loyalty & unrest   Plague virulence / lethality β and death fraction   Disaster frequency lightning, quake, flood, drought rolls   Bandit activity camp spawn & raid rate   House aggression loyalty drift & war appetite   Royal fertility dynasty robustness (low = succession drama)   Myth Off / Low / High

House { name, sigil, seatSettlement, loyalty, might, wealth, grudges{} }

Notable { name, house, age, sex, traits[2], spouse, heirs[], role, agenda, alive }

Caravan/Cog { origin, dest, cargo, value, path, departT, arriveT }

Prompt: ANNALS — a living kingdom in a single file

Working title behavior: the app titles itself per seed — "The Annals of Vaelmere", "The Annals of Osterholt" — because the central conceit is that you are watching a history write itself. The kingdom is the simulation; the Chronicle is the soul.

1. Vision

A procedurally generated fantasy kingdom rendered in real-time 3D that you can watch for five minutes or five hours. Zoom from a satellite view of the whole realm down to a market stall with laundry on the line. Time runs; harvests come in; caravans crawl the roads; a queen dies without a clear heir and two great houses raise banners; plague follows the trade routes; a dragon notices the treasury has gotten large. Everything that happens is written into a scrolling Chronicle in the voice of a medieval annalist, and a cinematic auto-director flies the camera to the story as it unfolds.

Four pillars, in priority order:

Legible emergence. Systems couple visibly: drought → failed harvest → hunger → unrest → rebellion. A viewer should be able to reconstruct cause from effect just by watching.

Zoom is the reward. Every altitude has something worth seeing — political geography at 3 km, trade arteries at 800 m, street life at 40 m.
The Chronicle is the product. Named people, named places, consequences that persist (ruins, grudges, epithets). The sim generates a story you could retell.
Watchable by default. With zero input it should behave like a nature documentary about a kingdom.
2. Hard constraints

Single HTML file, vanilla JS + Three.js from CDN (write against the r128 API surface so the same file runs as a Claude artifact during development and unchanged on Netlify). No build step, no framework, no backend.

Custom camera controller (no OrbitControls dependency — we need a bespoke rig anyway, see §5).

No localStorage / sessionStorage. Persistence is the seed: URL hash #s=1234567 fully determines the generated world. "Copy link" button shares it. Optional "Export chronicle" downloads a .txt.
Deterministic worldgen via seeded sfc32 RNG with separate streams for generation and history, so intervening in history never changes the map.
Performance floor: 60 fps on a mid-tier laptop at every altitude; <250 draw calls via instancing and merged geometry; graceful degradation, never a crash.
Everything procedural — no external textures or models. Vertex colors, tiny generated canvas atlases (windows, sigils), and shader work carry the visuals.
3. World generation pipeline
Runs once per seed, in order, with a brief "forging the realm" progress line:

Terrain. 6×6 km world. fBm heightmap with domain warping; one mountain spine, rolling lowlands, ~40% of seeds get a coastline on one edge.

Hydrology. Flow accumulation carves one major river (always) plus tributaries; lakes in basins; river mouths become harbor candidates.

Biomes. Moisture × elevation → meadow, farmland-suitable plain, deciduous forest, pine upland, rocky peak, marsh. Drives tree instancing, ground vertex color, and resource nodes (farmland, forest, ore vein in rock, fishing water).

Settlement siting. Score cells by water access, flat buildable area, resource adjacency, harbor bonus. Place 1 capital (pop ~2,500), 2–3 towns (400–1,200), 3–5 villages (60–300). Capital gets a keep on defensible high ground and a walled old core.
King's roads. A* over a cost field (slope² penalty, water crossing penalty that spawns bridges, forest penalty) connecting all settlements into a network. Roads are the circulatory system — trade, armies, plague, and bandits all use them.
Streets & lots. Inside settlements, organic street growth seeded from the road entry points and the market square; lots subdivide along streets; districts assigned (market, artisan, residential, temple, keep). Villages are a crossroads, a well, and a cluster.
Buildings. ~2,500–4,500 total from 12 archetypes × 3 tiers (hovel→timber→stone): house, longhouse, shop, smithy, mill (animated wheel on watercourses), granary, tavern, temple, warehouse, tower, wall segment/gate, keep. Procedural assembly: footprint, floors, roof style, chimneys, timber-frame overlay at tier 2+, hanging signs on shops.
Names & heraldry. One coherent phonology: places from syllable banks with earthy suffixes (-mere, -ford, -holt, -caster, -wyck); people from gendered given-name banks; great houses take a place or beast name. Procedural sigils = field color pair + one charge from a bank of 16 (stag, tower, wave, oak, wolf, comet, key, sun…), rendered to a small canvas atlas and used on keep banners, army flags, and UI chips.
The cast. Crown dynasty (monarch, consort, children) + 5 great houses, each holding a region and seat. ~100–140 living notables at any time (see §7).
4. Rendering, LOD & visual style
Aesthetic: illuminated-manuscript storybook. Low-poly forms with painterly vertex-color gradients — not flat-shaded minimalism, not photorealism. The world should look like the marginalia of a chronicle came to life. One directional sun/moon light with a tight camera-tracking shadow frustum (shadows fade out above 1,500 m altitude), height + distance fog for depth, custom gradient sky dome with sun, moon, stars, and the occasional comet.
Water: gerstner-lite vertex displacement + fresnel tint on rivers, lakes, sea. Rivers visibly swell during floods.

Day/night: full cycle; nights are deep indigo with warm emissive windows (per-instance emissive flag in the bubble band), pooled torch/lamp point lights (≤12), keep braziers.

Seasons (90 days each, 360-day year): global palette lerp + effects. Spring: saturated greens, snowmelt-fat rivers. Summer: warm golds (drought pushes to straw-yellow). Autumn: russet forest ramp. Winter: snow accumulation via normal-up whitening in the ground/roof shaders, snowfall particles, frozen lake tint.

Weather: clear/overcast/rain/storm/snow state machine; rain streak particles, wet-darkened ground tint, storm lightning flashes. Weather is mechanical, not just decorative (fire spread, battle modifiers, flood meter).

Ambient life: chimney smoke curls, birds (cheap boid flock), grazing sheep sprites near farms, banner cloth idle-wave shader, market crowd murmur of villagers in the bubble band.
LOD bands (camera distance to object):
Band Range Buildings Agents Detail     Far >2,200 m merged/instanced color-block masses per district armies → banner icon, caravans → moving dot settlement name labels, territory tint   Mid 500–2,200 m instanced archetype meshes full low-poly agent meshes instanced trees, roads, bridges   Near 120–500 m + chimneys, signs, timber overlays walk-bob animation wells, carts, market stalls   Bubble <120 m + per-instance window glow, laundry lines, lamps citizens spawn (≤80), individual heads turn prop shadows, torch lights
Citizens outside the bubble do not exist as entities — they're statistics (§7). The bubble makes the zoom promise real without simulating 8,000 pedestrians.
UI skin: parchment panel (#E9DCC3) with iron-gall ink text (#2B2320), crown-gold accents (#C9A227), house colors from sigils. Chronicle set in a period serif (IM Fell English or similar via Google Fonts, with graceful serif fallback); UI labels in a clean humanist sans. Trigger buttons read like acts, sentence case, active voice: "Unleash plague," "Bless the harvest," "Contest the succession."

5. Camera & interaction
Custom rig with three modes, all sharing one smoothed spring-damper transform:
Free: orbit + pan + scroll zoom along a curved altitude path — high altitude looks steeper (map-like), low altitude tilts toward the horizon (street-like). Zoom range ~5 m to ~4,000 m. Terrain collision keeps the camera out of the ground.
Follow: click any agent (caravan, army, notable, dragon) → low tracking shot with slight lead. Click empty ground to release.
Director: see §13.
Raycast click on anything selectable opens the Inspector (§15). Hotkeys: Space pause, 1–4 speeds, H hide UI, C Watch mode, Esc deselect.
6. Simulation architecture
Clock: SimClock in fractional days. Fixed-step accumulator; 1 tick = 1 sim-day of system logic. Speeds: pause / 0.5 / 2 / 8 / 30 sim-days per real second (at max, a year passes in 12 seconds — a monarch's reign in ~10 minutes).
System order per tick: Weather → Economy → Population → Politics → Military → Threats → Growth → Chronicle flush.
Render decoupling: agents store path + departure/arrival sim-times; the render loop interpolates positions every frame from current sim-time, so motion is smooth at any speed and nothing "teleports."
Stability rule: every positive feedback loop ships with a predator. Growth ↑ → land scarcity and food pressure. Treasury ↑ → dragon and bandit attention. Military strength ↑ → upkeep drain. House power ↑ → crown suspicion events. Target: after 200 unattended sim-years at defaults, population and treasury remain within sane bounds and the realm is still interesting.
Pacing target: a Chronicle-worthy event every 15–45 sim-days at default rates (tunable via the Disaster frequency and House aggression sliders).
7. Population & notables
Two-layer model (the Crusader Kings trick):
Pools: each settlement tracks population as a number with birth/death/migration rates modified by food, plague, war, prosperity. Pools drive building growth, levy size, tax income, and bubble-band citizen density.
Notables: ~100–140 named characters — the dynasty, house heads and their families, plus flavor roles (High Priest, Master of Coin, a famous smith, a bandit king when one arises, a prophet at Myth High). Notables have: age, sex, house, 2 traits (from ~16: bold/craven, just/cruel, shrewd/dull, pious/cynical, fertile, sickly…), relationships (spouse, heirs, grudges), and an agenda line. They age, marry (arranged for alliance value), have children, and die by an age hazard curve plus event hazards (battle, plague, childbirth, the occasional hunting accident, assassination). Deaths and births are Chronicle events; important ones are Director beats.
8. Economy & trade
Legibility over realism. Seven goods: grain, fish, timber, ore, tools, cloth, wine.
Settlements produce by geography (farmland → grain, forest → timber, ore vein → ore, harbor → fish; towns convert ore+timber → tools, capital produces cloth/wine), consume by population, and store in granaries/warehouses.
Local prices from stock vs. need; caravans (mule train meshes, up to ~36 concurrent) spawn to arbitrage price gaps along roads; coastal cogs (up to 8) trade between harbor settlements. Trade volume is visible traffic — the kingdom's health readable at a glance.
Treasury: crown taxes trade and harvests (default 12%); spends on army upkeep, disaster relief, bounties, rebuilding. Treasury funds war; war disrupts trade; disrupted trade starves treasuries.
Hunger cascade: food deficit → granary drawdown → hunger → mortality up, unrest up, migration out. Drought, plague, siege, and raided caravans all feed this one legible pipeline.

House loyalty (0–100 each): drifts with tax rate, shared wars, royal marriages (arranged automatically for alliance value; weddings are festival events), slights and grudges (event-driven), and monarch traits.
Unrest per settlement from hunger, taxes, war, plague, omens → riots (small fires, trade pause) → revolt (settlement flips banner) at extremes.
Civil war trigger: loyalty <30 on a house with military strength + a spark (succession crisis, famine year, tax hike, "Contest the succession" button). Houses declare for sides based on loyalty, marriages, and grudges. Territory overlay animates as banners change.

Phase Scope Acceptance     1 — The Land Gen pipeline, terrain/water/sky, roads & bridges, buildings + full LOD, camera rig, day/night, seasons, seed URL Fly from 3 km to a market stall at 60 fps; two seeds feel like different countries   2 — The Wheel Clock & speeds, economy, caravans & cogs, population pools, settlement growth/decay, HUD, inspector, Chronicle v1, Rates panel Left at ▶▶▶ for 10 min: visible growth, ≥15 chronicle entries, no runaway values   3 — The Crown Notables & dynasty, houses & heraldry, loyalty/legitimacy/unrest, succession, civil war, armies/battles/sieges, territory overlay, political Acts "Assassinate the monarch" with rival heirs → war within a sim-year, visible marches, a peace, and a coherent chronicle arc   4 — The Fates Disaster suite, bandits, dragon & Myth dial, omens, auto-director + Watch mode, remaining Acts/overlays, ambient audio (optional), perf pass The five-minute test

19. Acceptance: the five-minute test

Defaults, speed ▶▶▶, no input. Within 5 minutes a viewer sees: a season change; ≥8 chronicle entries including ≥1 named-character event; ≥1 visible incident (fire, ambush, omen, festival) that the director covers; and at least one district visibly grow. Within 30 minutes: a succession or a war. After 200 unattended sim-years: population, treasury, and house count remain in sane bounds and the realm is still producing story.

If the five-minute test passes, the thing is fascinating to watch. Everything above serves that sentence.

WEBGL PARTICLE CANVAS
Implement for each technical section canvas:
- Transparent WebGL canvas, opacity .4, mix-blend-screen.
- Use 240 points in a 24-column grid. Positions: col = i % 24, row = floor(i/24), x = -1 + col/11.5, y = -1 + row/5.5.
- Cap devicePixelRatio at 2.
- Vertex shader waves:
  wave = sin((p.x*6.0)+u_time*.7)*.035 + cos((p.y*7.0)-u_time*.55)*.028;
  p.x += wave;
  p.y += sin(u_time*.35 + p.x*4.0)*.018;
  gl_PointSize = 1.6;
  v_alpha = .12 + .12 * sin(u_time + p.x*4.0 + p.y*5.0).
- Fragment shader: radial point alpha via smoothstep, color mix vec3(.5,.5,.55) to vec3(.9,.9,.95), blend SRC_ALPHA, ONE.

GLOBAL GSAP SCROLLTRIGGER MOTION
- Register ScrollTrigger on load.
- Animate section h2, section p, .info-text, section ul li, .title-wrap h1 from opacity 0, y 40, filter blur(10px) to opacity 1, y 0, blur 0, duration 1.2, ease power3.out, trigger start top 85%, reverse on leave.

- Animate article img and .product img objectPosition from 50% 0% to 50% 100%, scrubbed from trigger top bottom to bottom top.
- Move all canvas backgrounds yPercent 30 with scrub 1.
- For the gameplay video element, ScrollTrigger from scale 1.15 and filter brightness(.3) blur(20px) to scale 1 and filter brightness(1) blur(0), start top 95%, end center center, scrub 1.5.
- Footer divs and form reveal from opacity 0, y 30, blur(8px) to visible, duration 1.2, ease power3.out, start top 90%.

IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
- Build the actual landing page as the first screen; no explanatory page, no placeholder boxes, no stock replacements.
- Use the exact text, assets, section order, IDs, and visual states above.
- Preserve responsive behavior: mobile hero is centered and dark-brown, desktop hero is split white editorial type; side nav hides on mobile; roster/table scroll horizontally where needed.
- All videos must autoplay, loop, mute where appropriate, and use playsInline.
- Hover states must remove grayscale/luminosity and increase clarity exactly as specified.
- Use CSS and JS safely in React effects with cleanup for event listeners, RAF, intervals, and ScrollTriggers.
- Final page should feel like a cinematic, technical cyberpunk game site with black/crimson base, white technical frame language, cyan navigation accent, and precise scroll choreography.

source_text:
AI Çağında THREE.JS:   

⭕️Bölüm 5

Three.js Game Skills: Codex ve Claude ile Playable Prototype Üretmek

Bu serinin kalbi burası. Çünkü artık tek tek sahne, kamera, input anlatmıyoruz; AI ajanına gerçek bir oyun üretim hattı veriyoruz. Majid Manzarpour’un threejs-game-skills reposu bu yüzden çok değerli. Repo, Codex ve Claude Code için “playable, polished Three.js browser games” üretmeye odaklanan self-contained skill’ler sunuyor. 

threejs-game-director ana giriş noktası gibi çalışıyor; gameplay, grafik, UI, asset generation, audio, debugging ve release verification işlerini ilgili skill’lere yönlendiriyor.

Codex kurulumu:

🔰npx skills add majidmanzarpour/threejs-game-skills --skill '*' -a codex -g -y

Claude Code kurulumu:

🔰npx skills add majidmanzarpour/threejs-game-skills --skill '*' -a claude-code -g -y

Bu komutlar repo README içinde doğrudan veriliyor.

Artık prompt da değişmeli:

Use threejs-game-director to build a playable futuristic hover arena game.

Requirements:

🔸playable loop first
🔸player movement
🔸enemies
🔸collectible energy cores
🔸score UI
🔸procedural arena
🔸desktop and mobile controls
🔸performance checks
🔸browser QA before final answer

Bu repodaki en güçlü fikir “önce playable loop” yaklaşımı. Görsel kalite sonra gelir. Önce oyun çalışmalı: hareket, hedef, risk, skor, kaybetme/kazanma durumu. 

Repo, agent’ın build, browser check, screenshot, canvas pixel check, mobile viewport check, ve QA gate çalıştırmasını bekliyor. Bu, AI ile oyun üretiminde ciddiye alınması gereken farktır. Çünkü birçok kişi “AI oyun yaptı” diye aslında sadece statik sahne paylaşıyor.

Beklenen doğrulama komutu:
npm run build
npm run dev

AI’dan ayrıca şunu iste:

Before saying done, verify:
🔸no browser console errors
🔸canvas is not blank
🔸player can move
🔸collectibles work
🔸mobile viewport is usable
🔸build passes

Repo ayrıca API key yoksa dış asset üretimini atlayıp procedural veya local asset fallback kullanmayı öneriyor ve API key’lerin browser-side game code içine konmaması gerektiğini vurguluyor.

Mini görevlerden göre beğen 🫠: Hover arena oyununu tek seferde “tamamla” deme. İlk promptta playable loop iste. İkinci promptta grafik. Üçüncü promptta UI. Dördüncü promptta QA. AI ile gerçek üretim böyle başlar.

📛DEVAMI GELECEK📛

title: 完整单文件 3D 小鸟闯关游戏
author: ivanainai
prompt:
Build a fully playable 3D Flappy Bird-style game in ONE complete, copy-pasteable HTML file using Three.js/WebGL.

Create an original, colorful bird and environment. The game should look beautiful in a screenshot and feel responsive when played.

Return the entire HTML inside ONE fenced html code block. The code must begin with <!DOCTYPE html> and end with </html>. Include all CSS and JavaScript. Do not provide explanations, fragments or additional files.

VISUAL DIRECTION

Create a bright, richly colored tropical coastal world with a turquoise sea, warm sunlight, soft white clouds, distant islands and subtle atmospheric depth.

Keep the foreground crisp and saturated. Use a carefully composed background with gentle parallax, leaving the bird and obstacles easy to see.

The hero is a charming golden-yellow 3D bird with an orange beak, expressive eyes, small animated wings and individually shaped tail feathers. Make it feel like a carefully designed game character.

Animate wingbeats, subtle body movement and a smooth change in body angle when rising or falling.

The obstacles are glossy emerald-green pipes with substantial rounded rims, visible thickness, convincing shadows and beautiful highlights. They must read clearly as solid objects with a navigable gap.

Use tasteful lighting, smooth geometry, soft shadows and restrained reflections. Preserve strong contrast between the yellow bird, green pipes and blue environment.

The opening screen must immediately show the finished world, the bird and several pipes. Keep the interface small and clean.

GAMEPLAY

Use a side-view gameplay plane with real 3D geometry and depth. Keep a fixed camera so the openings and collisions remain easy to judge.

Clicking, tapping or pressing Space makes the bird flap upward. Gravity pulls it downward between flaps.

Pipes move toward the bird at constant speed. Each pair has a gap at a different height. Award exactly one point when the bird successfully passes a pair.

Colliding with a pipe, the ground or the upper gameplay boundary ends the run. Show a short, clear impact response and a Game Over panel with the final score and a working Restart button.

Restart must reset the bird, pipes, score, obstacle sequence and simulation state without reloading the page.

Use these identical gameplay parameters:

Bird position: x = -4.5.
Bird collision radius: 0.35 world units.
Vertical gameplay boundaries: y = -5.4 and +5.4.
Gravity: 18 world units per second squared, downward.
Each flap sets upward velocity to 6.8 world units per second.
Pipe movement speed: 3 world units per second.
Pipe width: 1.2 world units.
Vertical gap size: 3.4 world units.
Horizontal distance between pipe pairs: 5.5 world units.
Gap centers vary between y = -2 and +2.

Use a fixed simulation timestep and collision checks corresponding to the visible bird body and pipe geometry.

Generate obstacle heights deterministically with a dedicated seeded random generator, starting at seed 42. Restart must reproduce the same obstacle sequence. Decorative randomness must not affect this sequence.

AUTOMATIC DEMO

Provide three small controls: Play, Auto Demo and Restart.

Auto Demo must play the actual game automatically. Its controller may only issue the same flap action available to a human player.

It must use the same gravity, obstacles, collision detection and scoring as manual play. It must not reposition the bird directly, disable collisions or make it invincible.

Aim for a smooth, watchable demonstration lasting at least 20 seconds. If the controller crashes, show the real Game Over state.

Pressing D resets the game and starts Auto Demo from the beginning.

Provide a Hide UI toggle that removes menus and buttons while preserving the score. This is for clean screen recordings.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

Deliver one HTML file that opens directly in a desktop browser without installation or a build step. A pinned CDN import for Three.js is allowed.

Generate all visible assets in code. Do not use imported models, image files, original Flappy Bird sprites or external fonts.

Compose primarily for a square 1080 × 1080 viewport, while supporting responsive resizing. Keep the bird and approaching obstacles visible throughout play.

Aim for crisp rendering and smooth 60 fps motion. Pause the simulation when the browser tab is hidden so returning does not cause a sudden jump.

If browser tools are available, inspect the rendered result and test manual flapping, scoring, pipe collisions, boundary collisions, Restart and Auto Demo.

Prioritize beautiful visuals, responsive controls, correct collisions and a genuinely playable game.

Return only the complete HTML in one fenced html code block.
