prompt:
Build a modern, responsive landing page for [PRODUCT NAME].

Style: dark theme, bold hero with a gradient headline, 3 feature cards, pricing section, testimonials, and footer with social links.

Use Tailwind via CDN and create a single self-contained index.html.

Then:
1. Save it as index.html
2. Push it to my GitHub repository:
https://t.co/m3Tb0w02Fd<your-user>/my-landing-page
3. Deploy it to Vercel using my VERCEL_TOKEN secret
4. Return the live URL.
description: 来源原帖或作者回复中的公开建站与浏览器交互指令；保留原文，作者所述效果未独立复现。
source_text:
STEP-BY-STEP:

1. Sign up for CREAO
https://t.co/dwjWTI9aWS

Create a free account with Google or email. Once inside, open the chat workspace and confirm you can access Skills, Connectors and Secrets.

2. Connect GitHub

Go to:
Skills → Connectors → GitHub → Connect

Authorise your GitHub account so CREAO can work with your repositories.

3. Create your GitHub repo

Create a new public repository, for example:

my-landing-page

Leave it empty and copy the repo URL.

4. Add your Vercel token

Create a token in Vercel:

Vercel → Account Settings → Tokens → Create Token

Then add it in CREAO:

Secrets → Add secret

Name:
VERCEL_TOKEN

Value:
Your Vercel token

5. Give CREAO the build prompt

Paste this into the CREAO chat:

"Build a modern, responsive landing page for [PRODUCT NAME].

Style: dark theme, bold hero with a gradient headline, 3 feature cards, pricing section, testimonials, and footer with social links.

Use Tailwind via CDN and create a single self-contained index.html.

Then:
1. Save it as index.html
2. Push it to my GitHub repository:
https://t.co/m3Tb0w02Fd<your-user>/my-landing-page
3. Deploy it to Vercel using my VERCEL_TOKEN secret
4. Return the live URL."

CREAO generates the page, pushes the code and deploys it.

6. Keep improving it

Once you have the live site, simply tell the agent what to change.

For example:

"Make the hero headline bigger, change the gradient to blue and purple, and add an email signup form above the footer."

CREAO can update the page, push the new version and redeploy.

7. Turn the workflow into an agent

Save the workflow as a reusable agent and add inputs such as:

repo_url
product_description

Next time, you can run the entire workflow from one prompt.

The result:

Idea → Landing Page → GitHub → Vercel → Live URL

The point isn't just creating a landing page.

It's learning how to turn an idea into something people can actually visit.

Watch the video, follow the steps, and build your own.

CREAO:
https://t.co/dwjWTI9aWS

title: 建站需求与信息采集
author: FreeSites_com
prompt:
I'm building a website for [BUSINESS].
The business sells: [PRODUCT/SERVICE]
Ideal customer: [CUSTOMER]
Location/service area: [LOCATION]
Primary goal: [CALL / BOOK / BUY / EMAIL / VISIT]
Main offer: [OFFER]
Pages needed: [HOME / ABOUT / SERVICES / CONTACT / ETC.]

Before building anything, act as my website strategist. Recommend the simplest site structure necessary to convert visitors into customers. Tell me what information you're missing and ask me questions one at a time.

Do not invent testimonials, statistics, prices, certifications or facts about my business.
description: 来源原帖或作者回复中的公开建站与浏览器交互指令；保留原文，作者所述效果未独立复现。
source_text:
How to Build Your First AI Website for FREE — 
No Experience Needed

You don't need to know how to code. You don't need to understand GitHub before you start.  And you don't need to pay someone thousands of dollars just to see whether AI can build the website you have in mind.

You need an idea, an AI tool, and the right instructions.

Here's a simple way to go from a blank screen to a real website.
1. Start with the website brief — not the website
Before asking AI to build anything, tell it what the website needs to accomplish.
Copy this:
I'm building a website for [BUSINESS].
The business sells: [PRODUCT/SERVICE]
Ideal customer: [CUSTOMER]
Location/service area: [LOCATION]
Primary goal: [CALL / BOOK / BUY / EMAIL / VISIT]
Main offer: [OFFER]
Pages needed: [HOME / ABOUT / SERVICES / CONTACT / ETC.]

Before building anything, act as my website strategist. Recommend the simplest site structure necessary to convert visitors into customers. Tell me what information you're missing and ask me questions one at a time.

Do not invent testimonials, statistics, prices, certifications or facts about my business. 
Answer the questions yourself.

Your knowledge + AI is much better than letting AI invent a business for you.

2. Make AI create the website plan before it creates the website
Once the brief is finished, paste:
Using my approved information, create the complete plan for my website.  Give me: sitemap and navigation
purpose of every page
homepage section order
primary call to action
copy for each section
suggested images/visuals
mobile considerations
basic SEO title and description for every page

Write clearly for a real customer. Avoid generic AI buzzwords and exaggerated claims.  Show me the plan before building anything  . Read it.  Change what you don't like.  Then say:

This is now my approved website plan. Do not change the approved copy, structure or claims without asking me first.  That one sentence can save considerable frustration later.

3. Give AI a design direction
Don't prompt:“Make me a beautiful modern website.” That gives AI permission to decide what beautiful means.   Instead, find 3–10 websites you genuinely like. Screenshots work.  Upload them and say:
Study these examples and identify what I appear to prefer in: 
typography
colors
spacing
navigation
buttons
photography
page layout
corners, borders and shadows

Don't copy these websites. Create a simple original design system inspired by the characteristics I like. Show me the proposed design system before building the website.
Now you're directing the AI instead of letting it direct you.

4. Build Version 1
You can experiment with tools such as ChatGPT/Codex, Claude, Lovable, Bolt, Replit and other AI website builders.  The tools change rapidly.  The important thing is the instruction. Give your builder the approved brief + approved copy + approved design system, then:
Build Version 1 of this website.  Follow my approved website plan and design system.  Preserve my approved wording.  Make the site responsive for desktop and mobile.  Make the primary CTA obvious.  Do not invent business information.  Do not add paid services, databases or dependencies unless they're actually necessary.  Show me a working preview before publishing anything.  You now have something concrete to improve.Don't try to make V1 perfect.

5. Don't confuse a preview with a website
This catches beginners .A beautiful AI preview isn't necessarily a finished website.Before calling it done, check:
□ Does it work on your phone?
 □ Does every button work?
 □ Does click-to-call actually call?
 □ Does the contact form actually send somewhere?
 □ Did you submit a REAL test lead?
 □ Are the images correct?
 □ Are the business facts correct?
 □ Is there a useful page title and description?
 □ Is the website publicly accessible without logging in?AI saying “implemented” isn't the test.
You clicking it is.

6. Own your website
Here's where words such as GitHub scare beginners.  They scared me too. The simple version:                             AI builder = where you make it.  
GitHub = where you can keep the website's code and its history.  
Netlify/Vercel/Cloudflare = places that can publish that code on the Internet.  
Your domain = the address people type to reach it.           

For a simple site, I like the idea of maintaining an independent copy of the code rather than having the only copy trapped inside an AI conversation or temporary preview.    

Ask your AI:
Explain how I can export or save this website's source code.  I am a beginner.   Walk me through saving it to GitHub and publishing it using an appropriate hosting service such as Netlify, Vercel or Cloudflare.  
Explain one step at a time.   
Do not change my DNS, deploy to production or delete anything without asking for my approval first.  

You don't need to become a Git expert. 
Think:Repository = website + history.
 Commit = checkpoint.
 Branch = safe experiment.
 Deploy = put it on the Internet.
 Rollback = go back to something that worked.
That's enough to begin.

7. The most important prompt may come AFTER you've built it
This is one we learned the hard way. Once your website looks good, AI can become dangerous.  You ask:“Could you just change this one thing?”  And it changes six. 

Before future edits, paste this:
MINIMUM-DIFF MODE. This is an approved working website. Make ONLY the change I specifically request. Preserve all approved copy, design, images, pages, URLs, responsive behavior and functionality that I did not ask you to change. Do not redesign, refactor, reorganize, rename, replace assets, update dependencies or “clean up” unrelated code.  Before changing anything, tell me exactly what you intend to change.  Afterward, test the change and report exactly what files were modified.  Then STOP.  

AI has made building Version 1 remarkably easy. Protecting Version 16 while creating Version 17 is the next skill worth learning.

8. Finally: launch like a customer
Open the live website on your phone.  Open it in a private/incognito browser.Pretend you've never seen it. Can you understand what the business does in five seconds? Can you call? Can you book? Can you submit the form? Can you find the address? Can you buy, if that's the objective? Then make one real test conversion yourself. 

Because the goal isn't: “I built an AI website.

”It's:“A stranger can use my website to become a customer.”
That's the difference between an impressive demo and a working business website.

I didn't grow up with computers.  I still spend plenty of time asking AI to explain technical things to me in plain English.  So if GitHub, DNS, hosting or coding sounds intimidating, don't let that stop you. If you can copy, paste, ask questions and check the result, you can start.  
Save this article and try the prompts. We'll keep testing the new tools and sharing what actually works.  
And if you'd rather skip all of this: Do it this way — or we'll build it for you FREE.
FreeSites— Jeff from FreeSites

You don't need to know how to code. You don't need to understand GitHub before you start.  And you don't need to pay someone thousands of dollars just to see whether AI can build the website you have in mind.

You need an idea, an AI tool, and the right instructions.

Here's a simple way to go from a blank screen to a real website.
1. Start with the website brief — not the website
Before asking AI to build anything, tell it what the website needs to accomplish.
Copy this:
I'm building a website for [BUSINESS].
The business sells: [PRODUCT/SERVICE]
Ideal customer: [CUSTOMER]
Location/service area: [LOCATION]

Main offer: [OFFER]
Pages needed: [HOME / ABOUT / SERVICES / CONTACT / ETC.]

Before building anything, act as my website strategist. Recommend the simplest site structure necessary to convert visitors into customers. Tell me what information you're missing and ask me questions one at a time.

Do not invent testimonials, statistics, prices, certifications or facts about my business. 
Answer the questions yourself.

Your knowledge + AI is much better than letting AI invent a business for you.

2. Make AI create the website plan before it creates the website
Once the brief is finished, paste:
Using my approved information, create the complete plan for my website.  Give me: sitemap and navigation
purpose of every page
homepage section order
primary call to action
copy for each section
suggested images/visuals
mobile considerations
basic SEO title and description for every page

Write clearly for a real customer. Avoid generic AI buzzwords and exaggerated claims.  Show me the plan before building anything  . Read it.  Change what you don't like.  Then say:

This is now my approved website plan. Do not change the approved copy, structure or claims without asking me first.  That one sentence can save considerable frustration later.

3. Give AI a design direction
Don't prompt:“Make me a beautiful modern website.” That gives AI permission to decide what beautiful means.   Instead, find 3–10 websites you genuinely like. Screenshots work.  Upload them and say:
Study these examples and identify what I appear to prefer in: 
typography
colors
spacing
navigation
buttons
photography
page layout
corners, borders and shadows

Don't copy these websites. Create a simple original design system inspired by the characteristics I like. Show me the proposed design system before building the website.
Now you're directing the AI instead of letting it direct you.

4. Build Version 1
You can experiment with tools such as ChatGPT/Codex, Claude, Lovable, Bolt, Replit and other AI website builders.  The tools change rapidly.  The important thing is the instruction. Give your builder the approved brief + approved copy + approved design system, then:
Build Version 1 of this website.  Follow my approved website plan and design system.  Preserve my approved wording.  Make the site responsive for desktop and mobile.  Make the primary CTA obvious.  Do not invent business information.  Do not add paid services, databases or dependencies unless they're actually necessary.  Show me a working preview before publishing anything.  You now have something concrete to improve.Don't try to make V1 perfect.

□ Does it work on your phone?

 □ Does click-to-call actually call?
 □ Does the contact form actually send somewhere?
 □ Did you submit a REAL test lead?
 □ Are the images correct?
 □ Are the business facts correct?
 □ Is there a useful page title and description?
 □ Is the website publicly accessible without logging in?AI saying “implemented” isn't the test.
You clicking it is.

Here's where words such as GitHub scare beginners.  They scared me too. The simple version:                             AI builder = where you make it.  
GitHub = where you can keep the website's code and its history.  
Netlify/Vercel/Cloudflare = places that can publish that code on the Internet.  
Your domain = the address people type to reach it.           

For a simple site, I like the idea of maintaining an independent copy of the code rather than having the only copy trapped inside an AI conversation or temporary preview.

Explain how I can export or save this website's source code.  I am a beginner.   Walk me through saving it to GitHub and publishing it using an appropriate hosting service such as Netlify, Vercel or Cloudflare.  
Explain one step at a time.   
Do not change my DNS, deploy to production or delete anything without asking for my approval first.  

You don't need to become a Git expert. 
Think:Repository = website + history.
 Commit = checkpoint.
 Branch = safe experiment.
 Deploy = put it on the Internet.
 Rollback = go back to something that worked.
That's enough to begin.

MINIMUM-DIFF MODE. This is an approved working website. Make ONLY the change I specifically request. Preserve all approved copy, design, images, pages, URLs, responsive behavior and functionality that I did not ask you to change. Do not redesign, refactor, reorganize, rename, replace assets, update dependencies or “clean up” unrelated code.  Before changing anything, tell me exactly what you intend to change.  Afterward, test the change and report exactly what files were modified.  Then STOP.

Can you submit the form? Can you find the address? Can you buy, if that's the objective? Then make one real test conversion yourself. 

Because the goal isn't: “I built an AI website.

”It's:“A stranger can use my website to become a customer.”
That's the difference between an impressive demo and a working business website.
